attacks.claim: Dark mode breaks the main content. `.day-card` hard-codes a white background, but the dark-mode block flips `--text` to near-white, so day headings and tile titles render light-on-white for the ~30% of users with dark OS mode.
QA covers only light mode and two viewports. Dark mode, the 360px low end of the stated mobile range, and Android are untested, so the 'pass' verdict does not cover the cases most likely to fail.
attacks.evidence: Visual QA vs Figma: Chrome 1440px (light), Safari iPhone 14 (light) — pass, pixel diffs < 1%.

attacks.claim: In dark mode, muted metadata text sits on the hard-coded white card, which gives roughly 2.4:1 contrast and fails WCAG AA for the time/meta text. The shipped contrast tokens were never checked against the card surface.
attacks.evidence: .tile .meta { color: var(--muted); } with dark --muted: #a1a1a6 inside .day-card { background: #ffffff; }

attacks.claim: The redesign removes the action users perform most (about 9.4 times per week) and replaces it with a bulk action that cannot add a single recipe. This solves the clutter goal by cutting the top workflow, not by serving it.
attacks.evidence: Most frequent planner action: adding a planned recipe's ingredients to the shopping list (avg 9.4 times/week ...) ... The old tile-level "+ List" button is removed to declutter tiles.

attacks.claim: Adding one recipe's ingredients now takes about six steps across three screens, with a servings sheet on the path. For the 64% of shopping-list additions that happen on mobile, this is a large regression in friction and latency.
attacks.evidence: tap the tile → recipe page → "Ingredients" tab → choose servings in the servings sheet → "Add to list" → toast with "Undo"

attacks.claim: The 72px fixed action bar on mobile has no bottom padding or spacer on `.planner`, so the last day (Sunday) and its tiles will be hidden behind the bar. Safe-area insets for iOS home indicators are also not handled.
attacks.evidence: .action-bar { position: fixed; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; height: 72px; ... } and "Sunday is the last child of .planner" with no padding-bottom rule

attacks.claim: The rollout goes straight to 100% of web users with no staged ramp for a full redesign, despite the known dark-mode defect. The claim that the flag-off rollback is safe ('same API, no data migration') is asserted without evidence, even though drag-moves and bulk generation are new write paths.
attacks.evidence: Ship to 100% Tue 10:00 PT behind `planner_v7`; old planner remains available by flipping the flag off (same API, no data migration).

attacks.claim: 'Generate shopping list' writes every planned recipe's ingredients in one action with no stated undo, dedupe, or merge behaviour. Users who already have items on the list could get duplicates or unwanted bulk additions with no easy reversal.
attacks.evidence: "Generate shopping list" (adds all planned recipes for the week) — ABSENT: undo, duplicate handling, confirmation

attacks.claim: One tap fans out to up to 21 recipes and their ingredient lists. The artifact does not say whether this is batched or sequential, or how it behaves on slow mobile networks.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: batching/request strategy for "adds all planned recipes for the week"

attacks.claim: Lens checked: no finding. No token, compute, or per-request spend is introduced beyond the planner's existing shopping-list writes.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: any new paid API or spend-bearing path in the artifact

attacks.claim: Lens checked: no finding in the shown markup. Recipe titles and meta text are rendered as normal text nodes, and no untrusted input reaches a write or exec path in the shown code.
The 'Share plan' action has no specified scope, link visibility, expiry, or consent. Sharing a personal weekly meal plan could expose more personal data than intended.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: share mechanism, visibility, expiry for "Share plan"

attacks.claim: Lens checked: no finding. The artifact introduces no new vendor, data residency, or lock-in dependency.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: any new third-party provider in the artifact

attacks.claim: The watch list has no alert thresholds, owners, or rollback triggers. 'Watch' without them does not define when the flag gets flipped off.
attacks.evidence: Watch: planner page JS errors, shopping-list additions/WAU, planner bounce rate.

attacks.claim: The tile's tap target is undefined. The h3 is not described as a link, and tap-to-open conflicts with drag-to-move on touch devices, where the artifact gives no gesture rules.
attacks.evidence: tap the tile → recipe page; Drag a recipe tile between days to move it.

attacks.claim: Up to 21 'Swap' buttons share the same accessible name with no day or recipe context, which is confusing for screen-reader users. Touch users also have no non-drag way to move a tile.
attacks.evidence: <button class="btn-ghost">Swap</button> (no aria-label) and "Move to…" only in the overflow menu for keyboard and screen-reader users

attacks.claim: The Lighthouse accessibility score of 100 is presented as support for the release, but it is almost certainly from light mode and does not match the dark-mode contrast problem.
Lens checked: no finding. No regulated data, licensing, or platform-policy change is evident in the artifact.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: any regulatory or ToS-relevant change

attacks.claim: Classes `.btn-ghost` and `.btn-icon` are used in markup but not defined in the shown styles, so the abbreviated CSS may not be the complete source of truth for the design system.
attacks.evidence: <button class="btn-ghost">Swap</button> and <button class="btn-icon" ...> with no matching rules in planner.css
